actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

device.name: MAMuJoCo coupled half-cheetah world (MuJoCo)
device.vendor: Christian Schroeder de Witt et al.

facts.text: The repository is a benchmark for continuous multi-agent robotic control based on OpenAI's MuJoCo Gym environments
The documented requirement is OpenAI Gym 0.10.8 and MuJoCo 2.1
The install_requires list is numpy, gym, mujoco-py, scipy, Jinja2, glfw and Cython: there is no serial, VISA, USB or vendor-SDK transport package
MujocoMulti reads scenario and agent_conf from env_args
For the coupled_half_cheetah scenario MujocoMulti builds the local CoupledHalfCheetah environment under a TimeLimit and wraps it in NormalizedActions
step maps the per-agent action blocks into one MuJoCo action vector and steps the wrapped environment
reset resets the wrapped environment and returns the per-agent observations
CoupledHalfCheetah builds gym's MuJoCoEnv from assets/coupled_half_cheetah.xml with frame_skip 5
The scenario observation concatenates qpos[1:] and qvel
The served model is the MJCF root '<mujoco model="cheetah">'
The default motor class sets ctrllimited true and ctrlrange -1 1
The model sets gravity 0 0 -9.81 and the integration timestep 0.01 s
The first cheetah torso has three root joints: rootx and rootz slides and rooty a hinge
The second cheetah torso torso2 has three root joints: rootx2 and rootz2 slides and rooty2 a hinge
A spatial tendon named tendon1 couples the sites t1 and t2 and is limited to range 1.5 to 3.5
The actuator block declares twelve motors, bthigh to ffoot on the first cheetah and bthigh2 to ffoot2 on the second
The twelve motors declare no ctrlrange of their own, so they inherit the default motor ctrlrange -1 1 of line 36

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge takes no seed input and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults (mj_resetData), so a run repeats on one engine but no seed selects a different state; the stand-in integrates its own placeholder motion

gaps: the multi-agent layer of MujocoMulti is not served: scenario and agent_conf partitions, per-agent observations, reward, episode limit and the TimeLimit wrapper are absent, and cap.world.step.v1 carries no reward, terminated or truncated; only the selected MJCF model is stepped

the upstream scenario CoupledHalfCheetah wraps this model in mujoco-py with frame_skip 5 and resets with N(0,0.1) noise on qpos and qvel; the bridge advances one physics tick per tick and resets to the mj_resetData model defaults

only the card's first model, coupled_half_cheetah.xml, is served; the manyagent_ant and manyagent_swimmer models, and the manyagent assets generated at construction, are other models and are not part of this driver

the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the MJCF for the joint layout, the actuator count, the per-actuator control ranges and the option timestep, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control value; contacts, friction, damping, gear, tendon and actuator dynamics are not MuJoCo's
the served model's spatial tendon coupling sites t1 and t2 is ignored by the stand-in
MuJoCo was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine or with the upstream mujoco-py scenario
no viewer, rendering, camera stream, reward or multi-agent observation is exposed: the package serves only the cap.world.* integration state and control vector
no physical robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
